correctness.rationale: From squarefree edge monomial unions F -> U(F), Boolean LCM iff each edge has a leaf endpoint: a nonleaf-edge collision is U(E)=U(E\{e}). Such an edge yields triangle or noninduced P4. Disjoint P4 supports give at most seven unions per three edges, hence density <=(7/8)^k even when other edges exist. At p~c n^{-4/3}, triangles and components with >=4 edges vanish in probability by first moments; number of P4 components has mean 12*C(n,4)*p^3 -> c^3/2 and factorial moments -> Poisson. Product decomposition gives (7/8)^Z and E -> exp(-c^3/16). Below scale first moment excludes obstructions. Above scale lower-couple to q=min(p,n^-7/6): diverging expected P4 count and o(mu^2) overlapping pairs force divergent vertex-disjoint packing; density tends to zero. Independent fresh edge-subset-union enumeration checked all labelled graphs on n<=5, counts of Boolean lattices 1,2,7,26,111; this finite check is not a proof of the n-limit.
